title: You can't hear a thing in here!
goal: At a noisy café, Sēf gets a call and a photo from Fahad; say what can't be heard, made out or seen
tip: Form VII in the present says what can or can't be done to a thing, with nobody named: iṣ-ṣōt ma yinsimiʿ 'you can't hear a thing', kalāmah ma yinfihim 'you can't make out what he says', ma yinshāf 'it can't be seen'. A feminine thing takes t-: ma tinshāf.
grammar: Form VII present as 'can / can't be done': ma yinsimiʿ, ma yinfihim, ma yinshāf
dialogue: A
فهد يدق علي، بس الصوت ما ينسمع هني
Fahad ydigg ʿalay, bas iṣ-ṣōt ma yinsimiʿ hni
Fahad's ringing me, but you can't hear a thing in here.
B
الموسيقى عالية وايد. اطلع برا وكلمه
il-mūsīga ʿālya wāyid. iṭlaʿ barra w kallmah
The music's really loud. Go outside and talk to him.
A
طلعت، بس الخط قاعد ينقطع، وكلامه ما ينفهم من الهوا
ṭilaʿt, bas il-khaṭṭ gāʿid yingiṭiʿ, w kalāmah ma yinfihim min il-hawa
I did, but the line keeps cutting out, and you can't make out what he's saying because of the wind.
B
طرش له مسج أحسن
ṭarrish-lah masij aḥsan
Better send him a message.
A
طرشت له، ورد علي بصورة. يقول إنه في المطار
ṭarrasht-lah, w radd ʿalay b-ṣūra. ygūl innah fi l-maṭār
I did, and he answered with a photo. He says he's at the airport.
B
راويني. الصورة مب واضحة! ما ينشاف فيها شي
rāwīni. iṣ-ṣūra mub wāẓḥa! ma yinshāf fīha shay
Show me. The photo isn't clear! You can't see a thing in it.
A
المهم، طيارته بتوصل الساعة عشر الليلة
il-muhimm, ṭayyārtah bitōṣal is-sāʿa ʿashr il-lēla
Anyway, his plane gets in at ten tonight.
B
زين! بنشوفه بعيوننا، أحسن من الصور
zēn! binshūfah b-ʿyūnna, aḥsan min iṣ-ṣuwar
Great! We'll see him with our own eyes; better than photos.
items: you can't hear a thing, the sound can't be heard
it can be heard: yinsimiʿ (ينسمع); a feminine noun: ma tinsimiʿ (ما تنسمع)
you can't make out what he's saying
what she's saying: kalāmha ma yinfihim (كلامها ما ينفهم)
you can't see a thing in it (a feminine noun: a photo, a room)
in a masculine noun: ma yinshāf fīh shay (ما ينشاف فيه شي)
the sound's loud: iṣ-ṣōt ʿāli (الصوت عالي)
go outside, step out (to a man)
to a woman: iṭlaʿi barra (اطلعي برا)
(recognise) il-hawa is the wind or the air
he answered me with a photo
it's clear: wāẓiḥ (واضح); a feminine noun: wāẓḥa (واضحة)
we'll see him with our own eyes

title: The ticket site won't let me in
goal: An hour before a football match, the ticket website is jammed; Sēf helps you get in, book and open your tickets
tip: Form VII present without ma says what can be done: yinfitiḥ 'it opens, it can be opened', yinḥall 'it can be sorted out'. From dashsh 'go in' comes ma yindashsh 'you can't get in': il-mawgiʿ ma yindashsh 'the site won't let you in'.
grammar: Form VII present as 'can / can't be done': ma yindashsh, yinḥall, ma yinfitiḥ
dialogue: B
سيف، موقع التذاكر ما يندش!
Sēf, mawgiʿ it-tadhākir ma yindashsh!
Sēf, the ticket website won't let me in!
A
عادي، المباراة الليلة، والكل قاعد يحجز في نفس الوقت
ʿādi, il-mubārā l-lēla, w il-kill gāʿid yiḥjiz fi nafs il-wagt
That's normal: the match is tonight, and everyone's booking at the same time.
B
وإذا ما لقينا تذاكر؟ شو نسوي؟
w idha ma ligēna tadhākir? shu nsawwi?
And if we don't get tickets? What do we do?
A
لا تحاتي، كل شي ينحل. جرب من تلفوني
la tḥāti, kill shay yinḥall. jarrib min tilifōni
Don't worry, everything can be sorted out. Try from my phone.
B
دشيت وحجزت تذكرتين! بس الإيميل ما ينفتح
dashshēt w ḥajazt tadhkartēn! bas il-īmēl ma yinfitiḥ
I'm in, and I've booked two tickets! But the email won't open.
A
يباله شبكة أحسن، بس في البيت ينفتح أكيد
yabā-lah shabaka aḥsan, bas fi l-bēt yinfitiḥ akīd
It needs a better signal, but at home it'll definitely open.
B
زين. والمواقف عند الملعب؟ بتكون زحمة؟
zēn. w il-mawāgif ʿind il-malʿab? bitkūn zaḥma?
OK. And the parking at the stadium? Will it be packed?
A
أكيد، يقولون باقي تذاكر شوي بس، يعني الملعب بيكون مليان
akīd, ygūlūn bāgi tadhākir shwayy bas, yaʿni l-malʿab biykūn malyān
Sure; they say there are only a few tickets left, so the stadium will be full.
B
عيل نطلع من البيت الساعة ست
ʿayal niṭlaʿ min il-bēt is-sāʿa sitt
Then let's leave home at six.
items: you can't get in, it won't let you in (a website, a place)
a feminine noun: ma tindashsh (ما تندش)
it won't open, it can't be opened
a feminine noun: ma tinfitiḥ (ما تنفتح); it opened: infitaḥ (انفتح)
I got in, I went in; you got in (to a man)
I booked two tickets; you booked two tickets (to a man)
try from my phone (to a man)
to a woman: jarrbi min tilifōni (جربي من تلفوني)
there are only a few tickets left

title: It's not your fault, son
goal: In Bū Rāshid's majlis, apologise for arriving late, accept his kind words and his lunch, and praise the food
tip: Form VII gives set phrases about people and things: inta ma tinlām 'it's not your fault (you can't be blamed)', ma tinwiṣif 'it's beyond words', ma tinradd 'it can't be turned down', kalām ma yingāl 'something you don't say'. With 'you' the prefix is t-: ma tinlām.
grammar: Form VII present in set phrases: ma tinlām, ma tinwiṣif, ma tinradd, ma yingāl
dialogue: B
السلام عليكم. السموحة يا عمي، تأخرت عليكم
as-salāmu ʿalaykum. is-samūḥa yā ʿammi, taʼakhkhart ʿalēkum
Peace be upon you. I'm sorry, uncle, I'm late.
A
وعليكم السلام. مسموح يا ولدي، الزحمة اليوم ما تنطاق
wa ʿalaykum is-salām. masmūḥ yā waladi, iz-zaḥma l-yōm ma tinṭāg
And upon you peace. No need, son; the traffic today is unbearable.
B
هيه والله، قعدت ساعة في الطريق
hē wallāh, gaʿadt sāʿa fi ṭ-ṭarīg
Yes, honestly, I sat an hour on the road.
A
انت ما تنلام. المهم إنك وصلت بالسلامة
inta ma tinlām. il-muhimm innak wiṣalt bis-salāma
It's not your fault. The main thing is you got here safely.
B
ما شاء الله، ريحة العيش ما تنوصف!
mā shāʼ allāh, rīḥat il-ʿēsh ma tinwiṣif!
Wow, the smell of the rice is beyond words!
A
تفضل اقعد. وعزيمتي ما تنرد، لازم تتغدى ويانا
tfaẓẓal igʿid. w ʿazīmti ma tinradd, lāzim titghadda wiyyāna
Please, sit down. And you can't turn down my invitation: you must have lunch with us.
B
أكيد يا عمي، ما أقدر أقول لا!
akīd yā ʿammi, ma agdar agūl la!
Of course, uncle, I can't say no!
A
وسيف يقول إنك صرت تطبخ أحسن منه، صج هالكلام؟
w Sēf ygūl innak ṣirt tiṭbakh aḥsan minnah, ṣij hal-kalām?
And Sēf says you've got to cooking better than him; is that true?
B
هذا كلام ما ينقال جدام سيف!
hādha kalām ma yingāl jiddām Sēf!
That's something you don't say in front of Sēf!
items: it's not your fault, you can't be blamed (to a man)
to a woman: ma tinlāmīn (ما تنلامين); he can't be blamed: ma yinlām (ما ينلام)
it's beyond words, out of this world (a feminine noun)
a masculine noun: ma yinwiṣif (ما ينوصف)
you can't turn down my invitation
something you don't say, not something to say
I'm late, I've kept you (all) waiting
to one man: taʼakhkhart ʿalēk (تأخرت عليك); to one woman: taʼakhkhart ʿalēch (تأخرت عليج)
the main thing is you got here safely (to a man)
(recognise) to a woman: il-muhimm innich wiṣalti bis-salāma
ʿēsh is rice in the Gulf, not bread
you've started cooking, you cook now (to a man)
(recognise) to a woman: ṣirti tiṭbakhīn (صرتي تطبخين)

title: They say we're moving
goal: At the office, Maryam passes on a rumour that the company is moving; ask who's saying it and say how far you believe it
tip: ygūlūn with no subject is 'people say, they say': ygūlūn ʿan il-mudīr innah… 'they say the manager…'. mithil ma ygūlūn 'as they say' brings in a set phrase. To doubt it: minu ygūl? 'says who?', and Form VII ma yinʿirif 'you can't tell, nobody knows'.
grammar: impersonal ygūlūn and Form VII ma yinʿirif: rumours
dialogue: A
سمعت؟ يقولون الشركة بتنتقل أبوظبي السنة الياية
simaʿt? ygūlūn ish-sharika bitintigil Abuẓabi s-sana l-yāya
Have you heard? They say the company's moving to Abu Dhabi next year.
B
منو يقول؟ أول مرة أسمع!
minu ygūl? awwal marra asmaʿ!
Says who? It's the first I've heard of it!
A
الكل يتكلم. ويقولون عن المدير إنه شاف مكتب هناك
il-kill yitkallam. w ygūlūn ʿan il-mudīr innah shāf maktab hnāk
Everyone's talking. And they say the manager has been to see an office there.
B
يمكن إشاعة. هالكلام ما ينعرف من وين يطلع
yimkin ishāʿa. hal-kalām ma yinʿirif min wēn yiṭlaʿ
Maybe it's a rumour. You never can tell where this kind of talk comes from.
A
يمكن. بس إذا صج، شو بتسوي؟
yimkin. bas idha ṣij, shu bitsawwi?
Maybe. But if it's true, what will you do?
B
من مردف لأبوظبي كل يوم؟ ما ينطاق!
min Mirdif l-Abuẓabi kill yōm? ma yinṭāg!
From Mirdif to Abu Dhabi every day? That'd be unbearable!
A
مثل ما يقولون، كل شي ينحل
mithil ma ygūlūn, kill shay yinḥall
As they say, everything can be sorted out.
B
إن شاء الله. بس لين يقولون لنا رسمي، ما بصدق شي
in shāʼ allāh. bas lēn ygūlūn-lna rasmi, ma baṣaddig shay
I hope so. But until they tell us officially, I won't believe a thing.
items: they say about him, people say he…
it's the first I've heard (of it)
as they say, like they say
UAE also: shrāt ma ygūlūn (شرات ما يقولون)
it's going to move, it'll move (a feminine noun: the company)

title: Checkpoint 4.1: late for the wedding
goal: Checkpoint: stuck in traffic with Sēf on the way to a wedding, say what you should have done, what will have happened by now, and what can't be heard
tip: Review of s4u001–014: hindsight with lō … chān + past (lō ṭilaʿna badri, chān wiṣalna), what will have happened with biykūn + past (biykūnūn bidaw), and Form VII for what can't be done (il-mukālama ma tinsimiʿ).
grammar: checkpoint 4.1: lō … chān, biykūn + past, Form VII 'can't be'
dialogue: A
الشارع كله زحمة! لو طلعنا بدري، جان وصلنا الحين
ish-shāriʿ killah zaḥma! lō ṭilaʿna badri, chān wiṣalna l-ḥīn
The whole road's jammed! If we'd left early, we'd be there by now.
B
جان قلت لي! أنا كنت جاهز من الساعة سبع
chān gilt-li! ana kint jāhiz min is-sāʿa sabʿ
You should have told me! I was ready from seven.
A
الحين بيكونون بدوا العشا
il-ḥīn biykūnūn bidaw il-ʿasha
By now they'll have started dinner.
B
وفهد؟ تظن بيكون وصل؟
w Fahad? tẓunn biykūn wiṣal?
And Fahad? Do you think he'll have got there?
A
أكيد، هو دوم بدري. دق عليه، يمكن يتريانا
akīd, huwa dōm badri. digg ʿalēh, yimkin yitrayyāna
Sure, he's always early. Ring him; maybe he's waiting for us.
B
دقيت، بس الأغاني عالية والمكالمة ما تنسمع
daggēt, bas il-aghāni ʿālya w il-mukālama ma tinsimiʿ
I did, but the songs are loud and you can't hear the call.
A
عادي، المهم نوصل قبل لا يخلص العرس
ʿādi, il-muhimm nōṣal gabil la yikhlaṣ il-ʿirs
Never mind, the main thing is we get there before the wedding's over.
B
إن شاء الله. بس المرة الثانية بنطلع قبل الساعة ست!
in shāʼ allāh. bas il-marra th-thānya biniṭlaʿ gabil is-sāʿa sitt!
I hope so. But next time we're leaving before six!
items: if I'd left early: lō ṭilaʿt badri (لو طلعت بدري)
we'd have got there, we'd be there (by now)
I'd have got there: chān wiṣalt (جان وصلت)
he'll have started: biykūn bida (بيكون بدا)
the main thing is we get there
the main thing is you get there: il-muhimm tōṣal (المهم توصل)
before the party's over: gabil la tikhlaṣ il-ḥafla (قبل لا تخلص الحفلة)
task: This week: with a tutor or exchange partner (search a tutoring site for «Emirati Arabic tutor»), tell the story of a time you were late, in about a minute. Then say what you should have done (lō …, chān …) and what the others will have done while they waited (biykūnūn …). Ask them about a time they were late, and use 3 items from s4u011–015 in your answers.

title: I gave it to him this morning
goal: At the office, Maryam is looking for the meeting-room key and a file; say who you gave them to and who'll give them back
tip: With two objects, the person goes on the verb and the thing on iyyā-: ʿaṭētah iyyāh 'I gave it (m.) to him', ʿaṭētich iyyāh 'I gave it to you (f.)'. A feminine thing takes iyyāha: ʿaṭētah iyyāha. The future works the same: biyaʿṭīch iyyāh 'he'll give it to you (f.)'.
grammar: double objects with iyyā-: ʿaṭētah iyyāh, ʿaṭētni iyyāh, biyaʿṭīch iyyāh
dialogue: A
وين مفتاح غرفة الاجتماعات؟ دورته في كل مكان وما لقيته
wēn miftāḥ ghurfat il-ijtimāʿāt? dawwartah fi kill makān w ma ligētah
Where's the meeting-room key? I've looked for it everywhere and I can't find it.
B
أحمد خذاه. عطيته إياه الصبح
Aḥmad khadhāh. ʿaṭētah iyyāh iṣ-ṣubḥ
Aḥmad's got it. I gave it to him this morning.
A
زين. والملف الأحمر؟ عطيتني إياه أمس؟
zēn. w il-malaff il-aḥmar? ʿaṭētni iyyāh ams?
OK. And the red file? Did you give it to me yesterday?
B
هيه، عطيتج إياه قبل يومين، تذكرين؟
hē, ʿaṭētich iyyāh gabil yōmēn, tidhkrīn?
Yes, I gave it to you two days ago, remember?
A
صح! لقيته، كان على مكتبي طول الوقت
ṣaḥḥ! ligētah, kān ʿala maktabi ṭūl il-wagt
That's right! Found it; it was on my desk the whole time.
B
الحمد لله. والمفتاح، أحمد بيعطيج إياه بعد الاجتماع
il-ḥamdu lillāh. w il-miftāḥ, Aḥmad biyaʿṭīch iyyāh baʿd il-ijtimāʿ
Thank God. And the key: Aḥmad will give it to you after the meeting.
A
بس أنا أبيه قبل الساعة ثلاث
bas ana abīh gabil is-sāʿa thalāth
But I need it before three.
B
لا تحاتين، الحين أقول له
la tḥātīn, il-ḥīn agūl-lah
Don't worry, I'll tell him now.
items: I gave it (m.) to him; you gave it to him (to a man)
a feminine thing: ʿaṭētah iyyāha (عطيته إياها); to a woman: ʿaṭētīh iyyāh (عطيتيه إياه)
did you give it (m.) to me? (to a man)
to a woman: ʿaṭētīni iyyāh? (عطيتيني إياه؟)
I gave it (m.) to you (to a woman)
to a man: ʿaṭētak iyyāh (عطيتك إياه)
he'll give it (m.) to you (to a woman)
to a man: biyaʿṭīk iyyāh (بيعطيك إياه)
he took it (m.), he's got it
I can't find it (m.), I didn't find it
a feminine thing: ma ligēt-ha (ما لقيتها)
a feminine thing: dawwart-ha fi kill makān (دورتها في كل مكان)
a week ago: gabil usbūʿ (قبل أسبوع)

title: Lend me a hundred?
goal: At a petrol station your card won't go through; borrow money from Sēf and promise to pay it back
tip: Money (flūs) is 'it (f.)' or 'them', so it takes -ha: barudd-ha lak 'I'll pay it back to you'. With iyyā-: baʿṭīk iyyāha 'I'll give it (f.) to you'. To borrow, ask sallifni 'lend me'; to a woman, sallfīni.
grammar: double objects: baʿṭīk iyyāha, barudd-ha lak; lending and borrowing
dialogue: B
سيف، البطاقة ما اشتغلت، وفي البوك عشرة دراهم بس
Sēf, il-biṭāga ma ishtaghalat, w fi l-būk ʿashara darāhim bas
Sēf, my card didn't work, and there's only ten dirhams in my wallet.
A
عادي، كم تبي؟
ʿādi, cham tabi?
No problem; how much do you want?
B
سلفني مية، وبردها لك باكر
sallifni miya, w barudd-ha lak bāchir
Lend me a hundred, and I'll pay it back tomorrow.
A
خذ. ولا تستعيل، ردها لي متى ما تبي
khudh. w la tistaʿyil, rudd-ha li mita ma tabi
Here. And no rush; pay it back whenever you like.
B
لا لا، باكر بعطيك إياها أول شي
la la, bāchir baʿṭīk iyyāha awwal shay
No, no, tomorrow I'll give it to you first thing.
A
زين. بس لا تنسى، ترى أنا بعد أنسى!
zēn. bas la tinsa, tara ana baʿad ansa!
OK. Just don't forget, because I forget too!
B
ما بنسى. والله ما قصرت يا سيف
ma bansa. wallāh mā gaṣṣart yā Sēf
I won't forget. Honestly, thanks a lot, Sēf.
A
ما سوينا شي. مرة ثانية أنا بقول لك: سلفني!
mā sawwēna shay. marra thānya ana bagūl-lak: sallifni!
It was nothing. Another time I'll be the one saying 'lend me'!
items: I'll pay it back to you, I'll give it (f.) back to you (to a man)
to a woman: barudd-ha lich (بردها لج); a masculine thing: baruddah lak (برده لك)
give it (f.) back to me, pay it back (to a man)
to a woman: ruddī-ha li (رديها لي)
I'll give it (f.) to you (to a man)
to a woman: baʿṭīch iyyāha (بعطيج إياها)
no rush, take your time (to a man)
(recognise) to a woman: la tistaʿylīn (لا تستعيلين); you'll see written لا تستعجل
(recognise) to a woman: mita ma tabīn (متى ما تبين)
how much do you want? how many do you want? (to a man)
to a woman: cham tabīn? (كم تبين؟)
because I forget too, mind, I forget things too
(recognise) tara at the start warns or explains: mind, you know

title: He still hasn't given them back
goal: On campus, tell Sēf a classmate still hasn't returned the books you lent him, and agree how to ask for them
tip: With a 'to' person and a thing, l- + person comes first and iyyā- + thing second: ma radd-li iyyāhum 'he hasn't given them back to me', biyrudd-lak iyyāhum 'he'll give them back to you'. Plural things take iyyāhum.
grammar: double objects with l- + iyyā-: ma radd-li iyyāhum, biyrudd-lak iyyāhum
dialogue: B
تذكر الكتب اللي سلفتها حمد؟ للحين ما رد لي إياهم
tidhkir il-kutub illi sallaft-ha Ḥamad? lil-ḥīn ma radd-li iyyāhum
Remember the books I lent Ḥamad? He still hasn't given them back to me.
A
من متى؟
min mita?
Since when?
B
من شهرين! والامتحان الأسبوع الياي
min shahrēn! w il-imtiḥān il-usbūʿ il-yāy
For two months! And the exam's next week.
A
قول له بصراحة إنك تبيهم قبل الامتحان
gūl-lah b-ṣarāḥa innak tabīhum gabil il-imtiḥān
Tell him straight that you need them before the exam.
B
قلت له مرتين، ويقول: باكر برجعهم لك!
gilt-lah marratēn, w ygūl: bāchir barajjiʿhum lak!
I've told him twice, and he says: 'I'll give them back to you tomorrow!'
A
عيل خلني أكلمه أنا. هو يسمع كلامي
ʿayal khallni akallmah ana. huwa yismaʿ kalāmi
Then let me talk to him. He listens to me.
B
زين، بس بأدب. هو ريّال زين، بس ينسى

title: Shall I show it to you?
goal: At the office, Maryam asks to see your presentation before the meeting; offer to show it to her and send it
tip: iyyā- works with other giving and telling verbs too: arāwīch iyyāh 'I'll show it (m.) to you (f.)', gilt-lak iyyāh 'I told it to you'. With a 'to' phrase, the thing can go straight on the verb: ṭarrshah-li 'send it to me', aṭarrshah lich 'I'll send it to you (f.)'.
grammar: double objects: arāwīch iyyāh, gilt-lak iyyāh; ṭarrshah-li
dialogue: A
خلصت العرض حق الاجتماع؟
khallaṣt il-ʿarẓ ḥagg il-ijtimāʿ?
Have you finished the presentation for the meeting?
B
هيه. تبين أراويج إياه؟
hē. tabīn arāwīch iyyāh?
Yes. Do you want me to show it to you?
A
أكيد. وطرشه لي بعد، أبي أقراه في البيت الليلة
akīd. w ṭarrshah-li baʿad, abi agrāh fi l-bēt il-lēla
Sure. And send it to me too; I want to read it at home tonight.
B
الحين أطرشه لج. شوفي، هذي أول صفحة
il-ḥīn aṭarrshah lich. shūfi, hādhi awwal ṣafḥa
I'll send it to you now. Look, this is the first page.
A
حلوة، بس الأرقام صغيرة وايد، ما تنشاف من بعيد
ḥilwa, bas il-argām ṣghīra wāyid, ma tinshāf min baʿīd
Nice, but the numbers are really small; you can't see them from far away.
B
صح، بكبرها. وباكر الصبح براويج إياه مرة ثانية
ṣaḥḥ, bakabbir-ha. w bāchir iṣ-ṣubḥ barāwīch iyyāh marra thānya
True, I'll make them bigger. And tomorrow morning I'll show it to you again.
A
زين. وتذكر الشي اللي قلت لك إياه أمس؟
zēn. w tidhkir ish-shay illi gilt-lak iyyāh ams?
OK. And do you remember the thing I told you yesterday?
B
هيه، حطيته في آخر صفحة
hē, ḥaṭṭētah fi ākhir ṣafḥa
Yes, I've put it on the last page.
A
ممتاز! جي المدير بيحبه
mumtāz! chī l-mudīr biyḥibbah
Excellent! That way the manager will love it.

title: My father gave it to me
goal: In the majlis, Bū Rāshid lends you an old book that matters to him; accept it with respect and promise to give it back
tip: Recycle iyyā-: ʿaṭāni iyyāh 'he gave it to me', ʿaṭētak iyyāh 'I gave it to you'. In fast speech the two objects run together: ʿaṭnīh 'give it to me' for ʿaṭni iyyāh. Learn to hear it; the full form is always fine.
grammar: recycle: double objects with iyyā- (ʿaṭāni iyyāh, ʿaṭētak iyyāh); fast-speech ʿaṭnīh
dialogue: A
هذا الكتاب عن الغوص، أبوي الله يرحمه عطاني إياه وأنا صغير
hādha l-kitāb ʿan il-ghōṣ, ubūy allāh yirḥamah ʿaṭāni iyyāh w ana ṣghīr
This book's about pearl diving; my father, God rest him, gave it to me when I was little.
B
آمين. ما شاء الله، شكله قديم وايد
āmīn. mā shāʼ allāh, shaklah gadīm wāyid
Amen. Goodness, it looks really old.
A
خذه واقراه، بس ترى هو أمانة عندك
khudhah w igrāh, bas tara huwa amāna ʿindak
Take it and read it, but mind, it's in your keeping.
B
يا عمي، ما أقدر آخذه! هذا غالي عليك
yā ʿammi, ma agdar ākhdhah! hādha ghāli ʿalēk
Uncle, I can't take it! It means a lot to you.
A
عشان جي عطيتك إياه. انت تحب هالسوالف القديمة
ʿashān chī ʿaṭētak iyyāh. inta tḥibb has-sawālif il-gadīma
That's exactly why I gave it to you. You love these old stories.
B
الله يخليك يا عمي. بحافظ عليه، وبرده لك أول ما أخلصه
allāh ykhallīk yā ʿammi. baḥāfiẓ ʿalēh, w baruddah lak awwal ma akhallṣah
Thank you, uncle. I'll look after it, and I'll give it back to you as soon as I finish it.
A
لا تستعيل. ولما تخلصه عطنيه، أبي أعطيه سيف بعدك
la tistaʿyil. w lamma tkhallṣah ʿaṭnīh, abi aʿṭīh Sēf baʿdak
No hurry. And when you've finished it, give it to me; I want to give it to Sēf after you.
B
إن شاء الله. بس سيف بيرده لك قبلي!
in shāʼ allāh. bas Sēf biyruddah lak gabli!
God willing. But Sēf will give it back to you before I do!

task: This week: search YouTube for «مسلسل إماراتي» (Emirati series). Pick 5 short lines where someone gives, lends, shows or hands something back (listen for إياه, إياها, عطني, رده). Pause, repeat each line twice, matching the speed. Within a minute you should hear شو / مب (UAE) or شنو / مو (Kuwait). If you hear سوف, ليس or هل all the time, it's fuṣḥā: pick another clip.
